knowledge-base.overview: Axum 0.7+ guardrails, Tower middleware composition, type-safe extractors, router patterns, state management, error handling, and testing for Rust web APIs. Loaded automatically when agents work on .rs files importing axum.

core-principles.principle: Axum is built on Tower. Embrace Service, Layer, and middleware composition. tower-http provides production-ready layers (tracing, CORS, compression, timeouts).
Use compile-time extractors for all request data. Never manually parse headers or bodies.
All handlers are async functions. Never block the Tokio runtime thread — use spawn_blocking for CPU-heavy work.
Compose routers with merge and nest. Separate public from protected route groups before applying middleware.
Implement IntoResponse for the AppError enum. Return appropriate HTTP status codes with consistent JSON bodies.

guardrail.rule: Never block the Tokio async runtime. Never call std::thread::sleep, synchronous file I/O, or CPU-intensive operations directly in async handlers. Use tokio::time::sleep and tokio::task::spawn_blocking.
Always implement IntoResponse for the AppError type. Never return plain strings or unwrapped Results from handlers. All errors must produce structured JSON with appropriate HTTP status codes.
Never leak internal error details (database errors, stack traces, SQL) to API clients. Log with tracing::error! server-side and return a generic message in the response body.
Keep handlers under 15 lines. Extract all request data via extractor parameters, delegate business logic to services, return the response. No business logic in handler functions.

AppState must implement Clone (Axum requirement). Use sqlx::PgPool directly (it is Arc-wrapped internally). Wrap mutable shared state in Arc<tokio::sync::RwLock<T>>. Never use std::sync::Mutex in async code.
Call .with_state(state) last, after all routes and layers are registered. State registration must be the final operation on the Router.
Always add TimeoutLayer to prevent slow requests from exhausting connection pool resources.
Implement FromRequestParts (not FromRequest) for extractors that only need headers or state. Use FromRequest only when consuming the body.
Layer ordering matters: outermost layer runs first on request, last on response. Always apply CORS before TraceLayer to include CORS headers in traced responses.

project-structure.description: Layered Rust project: main.rs thin entry point, routes compose handlers, handlers are thin, services hold logic, repositories isolate DB.
project-structure.example: myproject/ ├── Cargo.toml ├── src/ │ ├── main.rs # Entry point: env, tracing, bind, serve │ ├── lib.rs # Module declarations │ ├── config.rs # Configuration loading (env-based) │ ├── routes/ │ │ ├── mod.rs # create_router() — composes all routes + middleware │ │ ├── users.rs # User-related route definitions │ │ └── health.rs # Health check route │ ├── handlers/ │ │ ├── mod.rs │ │ └── users.rs # Handler functions (extract, call service, respond) │ ├── models/ │ │ ├── mod.rs │ │ └── user.rs # Domain types, DTOs, validation │ ├── services/ │ │ ├── mod.rs │ │ └── user_service.rs # Business logic layer │ ├── repositories/ │ │ ├── mod.rs │ │ └── user_repository.rs # Database access via sqlx │ ├── extractors/ │ │ ├── mod.rs │ │ └── auth.rs # Custom extractors (AuthUser, Claims) │ ├── middleware/ │ │ ├── mod.rs │ │ └── logging.rs # Custom Tower middleware │ └── errors/ │ ├── mod.rs │ └── app_error.rs # AppError enum + IntoResponse + AppResult alias ├── tests/ │ └── integration_tests.rs └── migrations/

notes.note: Handlers are thin: extract → call service → return response. Max ~15 lines.
Services contain business logic; they call repositories only.
Repositories handle database access only — no business logic.
AppError is defined once and implements IntoResponse.

routing.description: Compose public and protected route groups. Apply auth middleware to protected group only. Attach layers and state last.

handlers.description: Thin async functions: receive extractors, call service, return AppResult.

custom-extractor.description: Custom AuthUser extractor implementing FromRequestParts — used for JWT validation without consuming the body.

error-handling.description: AppError enum implements IntoResponse. Use thiserror for definitions. Define AppResult alias at crate level.

quick-reference.item: Thin async functions: extract → call service → return AppResult; max ~15 lines
AppState implements Clone; use sqlx::PgPool (Arc-wrapped); RwLock for mutable shared state
FromRequestParts for headers/state; FromRequest for body; custom extractors return AppError
merge for flat composition; nest for path prefixes; .with_state(state) last
TraceLayer + CompressionLayer + TimeoutLayer + CorsLayer on every production router
One AppError enum; IntoResponse impl; log internal errors; sanitize client messages
Never block runtime; use tokio::time::sleep and spawn_blocking for blocking work
axum-test for integration; mockall for unit; separate test database
